questions.question: Explain about the mechanism of water balance.
questions.solution_html:
• (5mks, 5mks)
  • Water balance in nutrition refers to the equilibrium between water intake and water output in the
  • body. It's a crucial aspect of maintaining overall health and preventing dehydration or
  • overhydration. Water intake comes from fluids and the water content in food, while water output
  • occurs through urine, sweat, breathing, and f aeces.
  • The body maintains water balance t hrough a complex interplay of intake, output, and regulatory
  • mechanisms like ADH and the renin -angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). These
  • mechanisms ensure that water levels in the body remain within a narrow, healthy range.
  • Fluid Intake
  • Thirst is a pr imary drive for fluid intake, stimulated by dehydration or increased sodium
  • concentration in the blood. The hypothalamus, particularly the osmoreceptors, plays a crucial
  • role in detecting these changes and triggering the thirst sensation.
  • Water Output
  • The kidneys are the primary organs for water excretion, adjusting urine concentration to reflect
  • the body's water needs. Antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also known as vasopressin, increases water
  • reabsorption in the kidneys, conserving water when the body is d ehydrated.
  • Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS)
  • When blood volume decreases, the kidneys release renin, which activates the RAAS. This
  • system ultimately increases blood pressure and sodium reabsorption in the kidneys, leading to
  • increased water retention.
  • Kidney Function
  • The kidneys filter blood and produce urine, a process that helps regulate water and electrolyte
  • balance. They can adjust the amount of water reabsorbed back into the bloodstream based on the
  • body's needs.
